items.bold: TRUMP EXTENDED CEASEFIRE INDEFINITELY — no end date, at Pakistan's request.
items.text: Trump announced via Truth Social Tuesday: the ceasefire would be extended until "such time as their leaders and representatives can come up with a unified proposal." No specific end date provided. Trump said the decision was made "at the request of Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, of Pakistan." He also cited Iran's government being "seriously fractured, not unexpectedly so" as a reason — signalling awareness of the IRGC vs diplomatic corps divide. Pakistan PM Sharif immediately thanked Trump: "graciously accepting our request to extend the ceasefire to allow ongoing diplomatic efforts to take their course." The extension removes the immediate war resumption risk — but without a deadline, it also removes the pressure on Iran to come to the table urgently.

items.bold: VANCE ISLAMABAD TRIP CANCELLED — White House said Vance held policy meetings, not travelling Tuesday.
items.text: Following Trump's ceasefire extension announcement, a White House official confirmed Vance would not be travelling to Pakistan on Tuesday — he had been spotted by CNN cameras departing the White House at approximately 6 PM ET after roughly 5 hours in the West Wing. "Additional policy meetings are taking place at the White House in which the vice president will participate." Witkoff and Kushner were also expected to remain in Washington for consultations. The White House said "any further updates on in-person meetings will be announced." This means round two of the Islamabad talks is on hold — with no confirmed date. Officials said a trip could be arranged quickly "if they receive indications that Iran is prepared to come back to the table."

items.bold: SECOND SHIP BOARDED: M/T Tifani interdicted in Indian Ocean by US Indo-Pacific Command.
items.text: The Pentagon confirmed US forces boarded the M/T Tifani — a "stateless sanctioned" oil tanker — in the US Indo-Pacific Command area of responsibility, "without incident." Ship tracking showed Tifani in the Indian Ocean approximately 400 miles southeast of Sri Lanka, heading toward Singapore. Satellite imagery confirmed the vessel was previously docked at Iran's Kharg Island on April 6. Tifani is sanctioned for conducting dark ship-to-ship transfers of Iranian crude oil in Asian waters. Pentagon: "International waters are not a refuge for sanctioned vessels." This is the second ship the US has physically seized since the West Asia War began — the first being the Touska in the Gulf of Oman on April 19. The Tifani interception extends the US enforcement posture from the Gulf all the way to the Indo-Pacific — a significant geographic escalation of the blockade.

items.bold: IRAN REACTION: "Extension means nothing — continuation of siege must be met with military response."
items.text: Ghalibaf adviser Mahdi Mohammadi (Reuters/CNN): "Trump's ceasefire extension means nothing. The losing side cannot dictate terms. The continuation of the siege is no different from bombardment and must be met with a military response." Tasnim reported Iran announced it would NOT attend talks on Wednesday, citing "an Iranian official." Araghchi on X: US blockade is "an act of war and thus a violation of the ceasefire" — the Touska seizure is "an even greater violation." Iran UN envoy Iravani: "As soon as Washington ends the naval blockade, I think the next round of negotiations will be held in Islamabad." Tasnim separately: Iran declared Hormuz water routes "closed until further notice" following ceasefire violations — a new channel Iran had designed for commercial passage is now shut.

items.bold: BRENT briefly topped $101 — first above $100 since ceasefire. Settled ~$95.
items.text: Investing.com confirmed Brent briefly topped $101 per barrel on Tuesday — the first time above $100 since the original ceasefire announcement on April 8 sent prices tumbling. This occurred when it became clear Vance was not departing for Pakistan and Iran confirmed it would not attend talks. Brent then retreated to approximately $95 after Trump's ceasefire extension announcement provided temporary relief. Saudi Arabia and UAE bypass routes via Yanbu (Red Sea) and Fujairah (Gulf of Oman) rising to 6.5 mbpd — up from 5.0 mbpd pre-war (ANZ). Gulf states producing 14.3 mbpd in April, down 3 mbpd vs March (Rystad). Bessent: Kharg Island oil storage "full in days" — the blockade is economically tightening.

items.bold: Trump advisers warning: indefinite extension removes pressure, allows Iran to drag out talks.
items.text: CNN (sources familiar with discussions): Trump's advisers "have privately warned the president that alleviating pressure could allow Iran to drag out negotiations." Without a new deadline, Iran has no urgency to submit a unified proposal. The open-ended extension reflects a genuine dilemma: a hard deadline risks war if Iran calls the bluff; an open-ended extension risks indefinite stalemate. Trump appears to have sided with Pakistani mediators who argued for more time. The US position for resuming talks remains: Iran must submit a unified proposal (implying sign-off from Iran's Supreme National Security Council, which needs IRGC agreement). Treasury Sec Bessent signalled the blockade will intensify, not ease — making Iran's precondition of lifting the blockade before talks even harder to meet.

items.bold: Hormuz stays restricted. Iran shut new commercial passage route after ceasefire violation.
items.text: Tasnim reported that Iran declared the new water route it had designed for controlled passage of commercial vessels "closed until further notice" following what it called US ceasefire violations. This shuts the alternative channel Iran had created post the brief April 17-18 opening — meaning even the limited navigation option Iran had previously offered is now gone. CBS News journalists confirmed the gridlock first-hand, posing as tourists to access the strait by pleasure boat: "dozens of cargo ships and tankers, all of which have sat idle for weeks." About 20,000 seafarers remain stranded on hundreds of ships in the Gulf. Including multiple Indian-flag vessels, crew, and the broader Indian maritime community. MEA back-channel with Tehran remains active. India-Iran relationship at maximum strain.

military.t: Bessent: Kharg Island Storage Full in Days. Blockade Economically Tightening.
military.d: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed Tuesday: oil storage at Iran's Kharg Island — which handles approximately 90% of Iran's oil exports — will be full "in days" as a result of the US naval blockade preventing tankers from loading. Once storage is full, Iran must either shut down production or find alternative ways to move oil — neither is easy. Iran earns approximately $140 million daily from oil exports; the blockade has zeroed this out. Bessent emphasised the continued US blockade and "other efforts to financially weaken the Tehran regime." This economic squeeze is the leverage Trump believes will eventually force Iran to submit a "unified proposal." However, Iran has access to a shadow fleet of tankers (Lloyd's List confirmed shadow fleet still moving) — the question is whether Tifani-type interdictions can shut that route too.

military.t: India: Tifani Seizure in Indian Ocean Brings West Asia War into India's Maritime Zone.
military.d: The M/T Tifani was seized in the Indian Ocean approximately 400 miles southeast of Sri Lanka — well within the Indo-Pacific theatre that overlaps with India's strategic maritime neighbourhood. US Indo-Pacific Command (not CENTCOM) conducted this operation, meaning enforcement has extended from the Persian Gulf all the way through the Indian Ocean. For India: (1) Indian shipping lanes between the Gulf and Indian ports now pass through a US enforcement zone; (2) Indian-flagged or chartered vessels carrying Iranian-adjacent cargo face interdiction risk; (3) India's Op Urja Suraksha warships in the Gulf of Oman are now operating in a zone where both IRGC gunboats and US destroyers are active. MEA channel with Tehran active. India has 280 seafarers in the affected zone and 8 vessels near the strait. CBS News confirmed 20,000+ seafarers stranded across the Gulf.

military.t: Indefinite Ceasefire: What It Means for India's Markets and Energy in Coming Days.
military.d: The indefinite ceasefire extension changes India's risk calculus: Immediate war risk reduced significantly — no resumption in the next 24-48 hours. BUT: (1) Blockade continues = Hormuz stays restricted = Brent $93-100 = India petrol/diesel hike pressure and LPG cut fully off table for at least 2-4 more weeks. (2) No talks date set = diplomatic stalemate could last weeks or months. (3) Tifani seizure in Indian Ocean = US enforcement in India's maritime neighbourhood — Indian vessels face proximity risk. (4) Iran shut commercial Hormuz route = even the limited passage Iran had created is gone. assessment.headline: DAY 53, 9:30 PM: CEASEFIRE EXTENDED INDEFINITELY. Vance trip cancelled. Tifani seized Indian Ocean. Iran: "extension means nothing." Brent briefly $101. No talks date. Stalemate. Infosys Q4 tomorrow.
assessment.body:
Tuesday 9:30 PM IST. The West Asia War enters a new phase: indefinite ceasefire stalemate.

WHAT HAPPENED
• Trump extended the ceasefire indefinitely — no end date — at Pakistan's request
• The extension will hold "until such time as Iran submits a unified proposal"
• Vance's Islamabad trip cancelled after announcement — spent 5hrs in West Wing
• Iran reaction: "extension means nothing" — Ghalibaf adviser Mohammadi
• Tasnim: Iran confirmed it would NOT attend talks Wednesday
• Iran shut the alternative commercial Hormuz passage route it had designed

THE SECOND SHIP — TIFANI IN THE INDIAN OCEAN
• US Indo-Pacific Command boarded M/T Tifani, 400 miles SE of Sri Lanka
• Sanctioned for Iranian crude oil smuggling via dark ship-to-ship transfers near Singapore
• Previously docked at Iran's Kharg Island on April 6
• This extends US enforcement from the Gulf to the Indo-Pacific
• For India: this is in India's strategic maritime neighbourhood

THE ECONOMIC SQUEEZE
• Bessent: Kharg Island storage "full in days" — blockade tightening
• Brent briefly topped $101 before retreating to $95 on extension news
• Saudi/UAE bypass rising to 6.5 mbpd — still 13.5 mbpd short of pre-war Hormuz levels
• Iran shut new commercial Hormuz route — even limited passage gone
• 20,000+ seafarers stranded across the Gulf (CBS News confirmed)
• Rystad: Gulf states producing 14.3 mbpd in April, down 3 mbpd vs March

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM
• Advisers warned Trump: no deadline = no pressure on Iran
• Iran's stated condition for talks: lift blockade first
• US stated condition for lifting blockade: final deal first
• Classic diplomatic deadlock — both sides need the other to move first
• Without a new deadline, this stalemate could last weeks or months

INDIA'S NEW CALCULUS
• Sensex 79,273, Nifty 24,577 — markets had already priced in extension
• No imminent war = positive for Indian equities
• Brent $95 persists = LPG/petrol relief at least 4-6 more weeks away
• Tifani seizure: US enforcement now in India's maritime zone
• Infosys Q4 results Wednesday = primary market catalyst now
• Rupee ~94.00 — stable but no significant recovery until Hormuz opens
• India buffer: 6-8 weeks crude, consuming daily

THE SCENARIO SHIFT
• War resumption risk: reduced from 40% to ~10% for next 7-10 days
• Diplomatic breakthrough: 25% (both sides still say deal possible)
• Prolonged stalemate: 55% — most likely outcome
• Iran escalation (Touska-type response): 10%

VERDICT: The West Asia War has shifted from acute crisis to grinding stalemate. No explosions tonight — but no Hormuz opening either. The blockade tightens. Iran hardens. Bessent says Kharg fills up in days. The question is whether economic pressure breaks the IRGC's resistance before Iran finds a way to keep its shadow fleet moving. India sits in the middle — relieved there's no war tonight, still paying $95 Brent, still waiting for its seafarers to come home.
